Market Intelligence Briefing
subheadings: 🇺🇸 United States  Bullish  Fed on hold / cyclical upturn
🇪🇺 European Union  Bullish  ECB on hold / sub-target inflation
🇨🇳 China  Mixed  easing bias / weak demand
🇵🇱 Poland  Bullish  easing pause / fiscal risk
🧮 Earnings Pattern — What the Market Pays For
Cash today beats AI promises tomorrow
🔍 Underowned Themes — Active on X, Underweight in Portfolios
Oilfield services for the Venezuela reopening
Quality software after the AI purge
Crypto winter turns into a credit event
AI debt supply meets a weaker dollar
🔮 Anticipatory Positioning — Markets Pricing In Future Events
US–Iran: talks or a second carrier
$AMAT  results land into a fab-spending upcycle  ↑
$COIN  crypto winter hits the income statement  ↓
Micron & SanDisk / MU, SNDK  "the memory squeeze"
Gold & Silver / GLD, SLV  "the safe haven trading like a meme"
Bitcoin dip-buyers / IBIT, MSTR  "buying the winter"
body: Thursday, February 12 2026 — Macro · Sectors · Flows · Crypto

Macro Stance: January payrolls rose 130,000 and unemployment fell to 4.3% CNBC [Feb 11], even as the benchmark revision cut job growth through March by 862,000 Reuters [Feb 11]. The January ISM manufacturing index printed 52.6% PR Newswire [Feb 02] while December retail sales stalled Reuters [Feb 10]: output is re-accelerating as the consumer cools, and the Fed has no reason to ease. Constructive on cyclicals, neutral on duration.

Rates & Curve: The 2Y closed at 3.52% and the 10Y at 4.18%, a 10Y−2Y spread of +66 bps — moderately steep, approaching the long-run average; over 20 observations the curve was little changed (2Y −1 bp, 10Y 0 bp, spread +1 bp), while over five observations the 2Y fell 5 bps and the 10Y 11 bps (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-11). The 3M bill at 3.70% still yields more than the 2Y, so eventual cuts remain priced (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-11). The S&P 500 closed flat at 6,941.47, VIX at 17.65 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11).

New / Most Important: Economists now expect the Fed to hold through May and worry that Kevin Warsh may prove too loose with policy Reuters [Feb 11]. That makes Friday's delayed January CPI Investopedia [Feb 11] the decisive print: firm core inflation hardens the pause, a soft reading revives the easing debate.

Playbook ✓: Own cyclicals — industrials, energy, staples retail — over long-duration software, and keep duration neutral with the 10Y at 4.18% (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-11). Add small caps only after a benign CPI on Friday Investopedia [Feb 11]. Cut risk if the 2Y climbs toward the 3.70% bill yield, a sign cuts are being priced out (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-11); add duration on a soft core print.

Macro Stance: Euro-area inflation fell to 1.7% in January Financial Times [Feb 04] and the ECB held rates, shrugging off the dip Reuters [Feb 05] — the reverse of the US mix. Equity money is following: Europe and Asia led global fund inflows as investors cut US tech exposure Reuters [Feb 06]. We are bullish on European equities, led by energy and banks.

Activity & Inflation: The constraint is the currency: EUR/USD closed at 1.1890, up 2.12% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11), importing disinflation and squeezing exporters. The DAX is down 1.7% over 20 sessions while the FTSE 100 is up 2.82% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11) — commodity- and bank-heavy indices are beating the export-heavy one.

New / Most Important: The STOXX 600 hit a record high as energy stocks surged while tech and financials stumbled Reuters [Feb 11], closing at 621.58, up 1.64% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11). Dassault Systèmes' 18% plunge on its outlook CNBC [Feb 11] shows the AI-disruption selling in software has crossed the Atlantic.

Playbook ✓: Own the STOXX 600 over the DAX; overweight energy and banks returning capital, underweight software, wealth managers and autos; hedge the euro on exporters rather than selling them. Change the call if EUR/USD extends its rally and the ECB turns to verbal pushback, or if inflation rebounds from January's 1.7% Financial Times [Feb 04].

Macro Stance: China is running two economies: a deflationary domestic one and a buoyant technology-and-export one. Consumer prices rose just 0.2% in January China Daily [Feb 11] and factory deflation eased more than forecast Bloomberg.com [Feb 10] — better, but still deflation. Property and household credit are not recovering, while AI equities and the yuan are strong. We are Mixed: positive on onshore tech and the currency, negative on property, autos and consumption proxies.

PMIs & Activity: The official manufacturing PMI fell to 49.3 in January Reuters [Jan 30], back below 50, so the producer-price improvement reflects anti-price-war discipline more than demand. Durable consumption is the clearest weak spot: auto sales fell at the fastest pace in nearly two years in January Reuters [Feb 10]. Confirmation of a turn would need the February official PMI back above 50 and Spring Festival spending that holds after the holiday.

Credit Impulse: The latest full-year print is weak: 2025 new bank loans were the lowest in seven years, and Reuters noted that more policy support is needed Reuters [Jan 15]. The feed carries no January credit print, so there is no evidence of a fresh impulse yet; January is seasonally the largest lending month, which makes the next release the key test. A rising share of household medium- and long-term loans would signal reviving property demand; short-term bill financing by companies would not.

Property: Property remains the drag. Shenzhen's government is drafting an $11.6 billion rescue package for China Vanke, according to Octus Reuters [Feb 10] — a firewall against a disorderly default at a large developer, not a demand recovery. A package of that kind does nothing for sales or prices, and the feed carries no sign of stabilising home prices. Avoid developers and mainland-property-exposed lenders until monthly price data show the decline narrowing.

Fiscal, Policy & Trade: Beijing is spending on hardware rather than households: China will invest 5 trillion yuan in the power grid over the next five years China Daily Global Edition [Feb 10], a multi-year order book for transformers, cable and grid automation. On trade, Europe is opening a door — Volkswagen's China-built Cupra Tavascan was spared EU duties on China-made EVs Reuters [Feb 10], a template Chinese brands will try to copy. Without a direct transfer to consumers, CPI stays close to zero.

Markets & Flows: The Shanghai Composite closed at 4,131.98, up 0.14% over 20 sessions, and the Hang Seng at 27,266.38, up 0.99%; ASHR is up 0.44% at 34.01, while KWEB fell 7.64% to 34.10 and FXI 1.94% to 39.47 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11). USD/CNY at 6.9106 is down 0.96% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11), with the yuan at its strongest since 2023 amid a report on Treasuries Bloomberg.com [Feb 09]. Flat onshore indices, weak offshore internet and a strong currency say foreign money is buying the yuan, not China platform equity.

New / Most Important: The AI rally has rotated to Chinese model developers: Zhipu surged 30% to lead Chinese AI stocks as a wave of new releases hit the market CNBC [Feb 11]. The supply-side counterweight is memory — SMIC says the industry is in 'crisis mode' over the memory crunch Nikkei Asia [Feb 11], which can cap hardware margins even as AI-software valuations climb.

Playbook ✓: Own the currency and the AI-and-grid capex chain, not the consumer: prefer ASHR to KWEB, keep developers underweight, and express reflation through USD/CNY downside rather than equity beta. Upgrade consumption names only if the February PMI returns above 50 and January credit surprises up. ⚠ Divergence: the yuan at its strongest since 2023 Bloomberg.com [Feb 09] contradicts a 49.3 official PMI Reuters [Jan 30] and the steepest auto-sales fall in nearly two years Reuters [Feb 10] — currency strength is a flow story, not a growth signal.

Macro Stance: Sanae Takaichi's landslide clears the path for tax cuts Reuters [Feb 09], and markets are reading it as disciplined reflation: stocks and the yen rose together. A Mizuho executive says the BOJ could hike as early as March and up to three times in 2026 Reuters [Feb 11]. That shifts leadership from exporters to domestic financials: Bullish, with a stronger-yen tilt.

Activity & Currency: The Nikkei 225 closed at 57,650.54, up 2.28% in the session and 7.66% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-10). USD/JPY fell 1.06% to 154.48 and is down 2.95% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11). Japan's top currency diplomat says officials are not lowering their guard against FX volatility Reuters [Feb 11] — a cap on disorderly moves in either direction.

Playbook ✓: Own Japanese equities tilted to banks and insurers, which gain from BOJ hikes, and trim yen-sensitive exporters; keep currency hedges partial. Add on a March hike signal that does not trigger a bond selloff Reuters [Feb 11]. Cut if USD/JPY rebounds toward its 20-session reference of 159.1790 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-01-14), which would mean the carry trade is rebuilding.

Macro Stance: The RBA raised rates in February — its deputy governor said changes to 'three key facts' prompted the move ABC News & Headlines – Australian Broadcasting Corporation [Feb 10] — and Governor Bullock says the bank will raise again if inflation becomes entrenched Reuters [Feb 11]. That collides with a softening household: spending fell in December after two strong months Reuters [Feb 08]. A strong currency and resilient banks against a squeezed consumer make this Mixed.

Demand & Financing: AUD/USD closed at 0.7075, up 5.85% over 20 sessions, and the ASX 200 at 9,014.80, up 1.66% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11). Banks are carrying the index: CBA's first-half earnings hit a record on market-share gains and the shares surged Reuters [Feb 10]. Higher rates widen margins now but raise mortgage stress later, so the bank rally is a margin trade, not a credit-quality one.

Playbook ✓: Stay long AUD/USD while the RBA keeps its hiking bias Reuters [Feb 11]; hold the major banks but take profits into strength; avoid rate-sensitive retailers and housing-linked names. Change the call if the next quarterly CPI undershoots or household spending falls again — either would remove the second hike and cap the currency.

Monetary & Activity: The NBP held rates in February (Bankier: 'Rates held — the NBP president comments') Bankier.pl [Feb 05], and the MPC projects inflation in line with the target, leaving the key decisions for March (Business Insider Polska) Business Insider Polska [Feb 06]: easing is paused, not over. The weak link is fiscal — Fitch says Poland risks a rating downgrade if debt is not stabilised Reuters [Feb 10].

FX & Markets: USD/PLN closed at 3.5462, down 1.96% over 20 sessions, and EUR/PLN at 4.2182 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11): the zloty is riding euro strength against the dollar. EPOL is up 6.37% over 20 sessions at 38.39 and the WIG20TR ETF 4.43% at 67.85, led by Orlen (PKN) at 111.90, up 13.77%, PGE at 10.27, up 10.69%, and Pekao at 230.30, up 10.14% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11).

Companies: Orlen shares are at their highest in years as commodities drive profits (Money.pl) Money.pl [Feb 10]. KGHM rose 5.06% in the prior session to 320.00, while PKO BP is down 4.33% over five sessions at 91.94 and CD Projekt 5.11% over 20 sessions at 241.20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11). Rzeczpospolita reports record billions flowing into funds as retail investors buy shares again Rzeczpospolita [Feb 11].

Security & New Development: The event risk is the CJEU ruling on WIBOR-linked mortgages, which Bankier dates to 12 February and frames as a possible breakthrough for borrowers Bankier.pl [Feb 09]; a borrower-friendly verdict would reopen legal-provision risk for PKO and Pekao. Global capital keeps coming: a FedEx- and Advent-led consortium agreed to buy parcel-locker firm InPost in a $9.2 billion deal Reuters [Feb 09].

Playbook ✓: Overweight Poland via EPOL, led by Orlen and PGE; hold banks at neutral into the WIBOR ruling and add if it is bank-friendly; leave the zloty unhedged while the dollar weakens. Cut the overweight if Fitch moves the outlook to negative. ⚠ Divergence: record retail inflows into funds Rzeczpospolita [Feb 11] run against Fitch's downgrade warning Reuters [Feb 10] — equity euphoria versus fiscal deterioration.

Narrative: Consensus still treats software as an AI beneficiary; the tape treats it as a casualty. XLK is down 2.4% over 20 sessions and Microsoft 14.09% at 404.37 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11), as AI-loser software stocks were overshadowed while hardware earnings jumped Bloomberg.com [Feb 11]. The open question is per-seat pricing once AI agents do the work.

Reported: Cisco topped estimates but dropped 7% on a mediocre forecast CNBC [Feb 11], and French software maker Dassault Systèmes plunged 18%, on track for its worst day ever CNBC [Feb 11]. Beats are irrelevant if guidance does not show AI lifting revenue.

EPS Upside Watch: Apple has the cleanest large-cap setup: AAPL is up 5.54% over 20 sessions at 275.50 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11), insulated by services and installed-base pricing. AI hardware, where the earnings jump is visible Bloomberg.com [Feb 11], is the other upside pocket.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Oracle and Palantir are down 22.31% and 24.18% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11): even AI-adjacent software is being sold indiscriminately — late-stage capitulation. Stay Bearish until a major software name raises guidance and holds the gain.

Narrative: Communication services split between ad and subscription platforms that monetise AI and capex-heavy giants that finance it with debt. XLC is down 0.13% over 20 sessions; META is up 5.96% while GOOGL fell 7.44% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11) after Alphabet sold almost $32 billion of bonds to fund AI Bloomberg.com [Feb 10].

Reported: Spotify shares jumped on strong earnings and subscriber growth WSJ [Feb 10] — subscription pricing power is being rewarded even as software is punished. Disney is down 4.3% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11).

EPS Upside Watch: Meta remains the upside candidate: its 20-session gain shows investors accepted its capex step-up, with AI-driven ad targeting the bull case. Spotify's price increases flow straight to margin WSJ [Feb 10], making it the cleanest beat-and-raise setup in the group.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Netflix is down 11.85% over 20 sessions at 79.62 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11): streaming is being de-rated alongside software rather than traded as a defensive. Mixed — own ad and subscription cash generators, underweight debt-funded capex stories.

Narrative: Financials should benefit from a firmer economy; instead AI-disruption fears jumped from software to brokers and wealth platforms. XLF fell 1.51% in the prior session and 2.75% over 20 sessions, with JPMorgan down 2.34% and Bank of America 2.78% on the day (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11). LPL closed 8% lower as the threat spread to financials CNBC [Feb 10].

Reported: Robinhood's stock plunged after Q4 revenue missed Wall Street estimates Yahoo Finance [Feb 11] — retail brokerage is the most exposed corner to the crypto slump. The newsflow is about business-model risk, not deposits.

EPS Upside Watch: Goldman Sachs is the best-positioned large name: GS is up 3.43% over five sessions at 944.59 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11), with underwriting levered to jumbo issuance such as Alphabet's bond deal Bloomberg.com [Feb 10] and trading levered to volatility.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The risk sits in credit, not deposits: Morgan Stanley warns the AI-led software selloff may pose a risk to a $1.5 trillion US credit market Reuters [Feb 10] — lenders to software companies. Bearish until that contagion is priced.

Narrative: Consensus says oil is oversupplied, yet energy leads 2026. XLE is up 16.98% over 20 sessions, Exxon 22.93% and Chevron 13.39% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11), and Europe's record high was driven by an energy surge Reuters [Feb 11]. The driver is rotation out of tech plus a Middle East risk premium, not the commodity balance.

Reported: TotalEnergies halved buybacks while keeping growth plans as low oil and gas prices weighed on profits Reuters [Feb 11]. European majors are protecting balance sheets; US integrateds lean on volume growth.

EPS Upside Watch: Exxon and Chevron have the most volume leverage: Brent at 69.40 is up 6.0% over 20 sessions and WTI at 64.63 is up 5.69% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11), and at current output every sustained dollar of price gain drops to free cash flow.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The EIA forecasts lower oil prices in 2026 and 2027 due to persistent stock builds U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) (.gov) [Feb 11] — the sector is rallying against the official balance. Bullish, but prefer US integrateds to payout-cutting European majors and keep trailing stops.

Narrative: Industrials are the physical leg of AI capex plus a cyclical recovery. XLI is up 6.6% over 20 sessions and Caterpillar 21.75%, including 4.4% in the prior session to 775.00, while the Dow closed at 50,121.40 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11). The January ISM manufacturing index at 52.6% PR Newswire [Feb 02] confirms the cycle is turning.
Reported: Caterpillar topped estimates as data centers boosted power demand Bloomberg [Jan 29] — the clearest evidence that AI spending has reached heavy machinery and on-site generation.

EPS Upside Watch: Power-generation and electrical-equipment suppliers carry the most estimate momentum, with data-center load the common driver Bloomberg [Jan 29]; Caterpillar's 20-session move says the market is still revising numbers up rather than pricing a peak.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Aerospace is lagging the cycle: GE is down 4.13% over 20 sessions and Boeing fell 2.61% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11). Leadership has rotated from aero to power and construction equipment. Bullish; overweight power-gen, neutral aero.

Narrative: The K-shaped consumer is now in the numbers. XLY is down 5.19% over 20 sessions and Amazon 15.88% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11) after an earnings miss and $200 billion capex guidance CNBC [Feb 05]. December retail sales stalled Reuters [Feb 10], so the sector has lost both its mega-cap support and its macro tailwind.

Reported: McDonald's beat estimates as its value push paid off CNBC [Feb 11] — traffic is going to the cheapest credible offer. Tesla is up 5.48% over five sessions while Nike is down 5.96% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11).

EPS Upside Watch: Value-led restaurants and off-price retail are best placed: McDonald's shows that value promotions can still deliver a beat CNBC [Feb 11] when they win share, and chains with scale purchasing can fund them without guidance cuts.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Home builder stocks are breaking out with the best start to a year in a decade Barron's [Feb 11] even as discretionary spending weakens — lower mortgage rates are beating the consumer narrative. Bearish on the sector, long builders as the exception.

Narrative: Staples are where the rotation out of tech is landing. XLP is up 8.99% over 20 sessions, Walmart 6.99% and Costco 3.84% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11). The driver is relative safety plus pricing power at scale retailers, not a revival in branded volumes.
Reported: Ahold Delhaize shares jumped after growth in US online sales WSJ [Feb 11] — the omnichannel-grocery formula that is also powering Walmart's re-rating.

EPS Upside Watch: Walmart and Costco: in a K-shaped economy the scale grocers can win share from both ends. Walmart's 1.63% gain in the prior session to 128.77 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11) shows the bid is still building after the payroll report.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Branded packaged food is not participating — retailers win the volume while brand owners lose it, which is why the rotation should be expressed through retailers, not consumer-products makers. Bullish on staples retail; avoid branded food until volumes stabilise.

Narrative: Health care is split between obesity-and-oncology growth and a managed-care margin crisis. XLV is down 0.31% over 20 sessions, but UnitedHealth fell 16.48% over 20 sessions and Lilly 8.3% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11).
Reported: Molina shares sank 28% on a surprise Q4 loss and disappointing guidance Yahoo Finance [Feb 05], confirming that medical costs are still outrunning premiums for insurers.

EPS Upside Watch: Large-cap pharma with volume growth: Lilly's pullback leaves it at 1,015.21 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11), with obesity demand still the sector's main earnings engine and the pullback offering a better entry than at the highs.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Managed care looks cheap after the drawdown, but Molina's guidance Yahoo Finance [Feb 05] says the cost cycle has not turned; the contrarian buy is premature. Mixed: own pharma growth, avoid insurers until 2026 cost trends are proven.

Narrative: Materials are a monetary-metals trade. XLB is up 10.03% over 20 sessions; gold closed at 5,098.50, up 10.86%, and Freeport is up 10.31% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11). Dollar weakness — DXY down 2.32% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11) — is the common driver.
Reported: Linde beat but its shares fell over 2% as 2026 guidance disappointed Investing.com [Feb 05] — industrial gases are a volume business that the metals rally does not help.

EPS Upside Watch: Gold miners: Newmont is up 8.7% over 20 sessions at 124.60 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11), and at current bullion prices margins expand faster than costs, which sets up upward estimate revisions through the next reporting round.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Copper is not confirming: it closed at 5.95, down 0.35% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11), even though it remains the AI data-centre and grid capex metal. Bullish on precious-metal miners, neutral copper until it breaks out.

Narrative: Real estate is a rate-stability trade with a valuation cushion. XLRE is up 4.57% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11) while the 10Y is unchanged over 20 observations at 4.18% (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-11), and US REITs ended January at a median 16.2% discount to net asset value S&P Global [Feb 05].
Reported: NNN REIT announced 2025 results and initial 2026 guidance PR Newswire [Feb 11]; net-lease landlords with fixed escalators are the template for steady cash flow in a flat-rate world.

EPS Upside Watch: Net-lease and data-centre REITs: a double-digit discount to NAV S&P Global [Feb 05] lets private buyers arbitrage public prices, which makes take-private M&A the likeliest upside catalyst.

⚡ Breaking Convention: XLRE slipped only 0.09% on payroll day (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11) — the market is treating REITs as value, not duration. Bullish while the 10Y holds near 4.18% (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-11).

Narrative: Utilities are now a political asset class. XLU is up 4.06% over 20 sessions and NextEra 11.91%, but Constellation is down 16.99% and Vistra 6.57% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11): regulated growth is being bought, merchant power tied to data-centre politics is being sold.
Reported: CMS Energy exceeded its 2025 earnings guidance and raised 2026 adjusted EPS guidance PR Newswire [Feb 05] — regulated capex is compounding as planned.

EPS Upside Watch: Regulated utilities with large-load tariffs that make data-centre customers pay for grid upgrades protect rate cases and earnings growth, unlike merchant generators exposed to price caps and political intervention.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Senators introduced the first bipartisan effort to curb utility-bill hikes related to data centres NBC News [Feb 11] — the AI-power trade now carries regulatory risk. Mixed: own regulated growth such as NEE, avoid independent power producers until the policy shape is clear.

Narrative: European autos face EV write-downs, tariffs and Chinese competition at once. The STOXX autos tracker EXV5 is down 3.01% over five sessions and 2.24% over 20 at 45.84, with Mercedes down 4.92% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11).

Reported: Stellantis shares slumped over 20% after a $26.5 billion EV-related writedown Reuters [Feb 06]; its US listing is down 25.51% over five sessions at 7.62 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11). The EV reset has become a balance-sheet event.

EPS Upside Watch: Volkswagen: its China-built Cupra Tavascan was spared EU duties on China-made EVs Reuters [Feb 10], cutting the tariff cost on an imported model; VOW3 is down only 0.14% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11).

⚡ Breaking Convention: The VW exemption Reuters [Feb 10] is also a precedent for Chinese brands to negotiate their way into Europe — the competitive threat rises as the tariff wall softens. Bearish; BMW, down 1.54% over 20 sessions, is the relative defensive (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11).

Narrative: Semis are the AI trade that is earning its multiple. SOXX is up 9.03% over five sessions and 8.07% over 20; TSMC's ADR is up 14.84% over five sessions, ASML 13.03% over 20, and Micron rose 9.94% in the prior session to 410.34 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11).

Reported: TSMC's January revenue jumped 37% as AI spending marched on Bloomberg.com [Feb 09], and its board approved a record $45 billion spending package for new fabs Tom's Hardware [Feb 10] — a direct order signal for equipment makers.

EPS Upside Watch: Equipment and memory: the TSMC capex vote Tom's Hardware [Feb 10] feeds ASML and the US tool makers, and Micron's surge shows memory pricing outrunning estimates. NVDA is up 9.11% over five sessions at 190.05 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Memory scarcity taxes the rest of the chain: SMIC says the industry is in 'crisis mode' over the memory crunch Nikkei Asia [Feb 11]. Bullish on memory and equipment, underweight handset and PC chip exposure that must absorb higher memory costs.

Rewarded: The market paid for visible demand and pricing power: CBA's record half sent the shares higher Reuters [Feb 10], Spotify jumped on earnings and subscriber growth WSJ [Feb 10], and McDonald's beat as value drew traffic CNBC [Feb 11]. TSMC's January revenue jump Bloomberg.com [Feb 09] kept the AI hardware chain bid.

Punished: Beats without guidance were sold: Cisco fell 7% despite topping estimates CNBC [Feb 11]. Weak outlooks were punished hard — Molina sank 28% Yahoo Finance [Feb 05] and Dassault Systèmes 18% CNBC [Feb 11] — and Amazon fell on a miss paired with a $200 billion capex plan CNBC [Feb 05].

Pattern: Two filters explain the reactions. Guidance beats the quarter: companies that raise or hold credible outlooks get paid, those that do not are sold regardless of the beat. And AI is a cost line until proven a revenue line — software and capex-heavy platforms are discounted, while hardware where AI already shows up in revenue is rewarded Bloomberg.com [Feb 11].

Attention into EPS: Applied Materials reports with traders positioned for a large move Investopedia [Feb 11], the first test of whether TSMC's capex vote converts into tool orders. Coinbase is also on deck, with JPMorgan cutting its target ahead of earnings CoinDesk [Feb 10] — a test of how much crypto weakness the stock already discounts.

Playbook: Buy beat-and-raise in hardware, banks and staples retail on the first pullback; sell beat-and-hold in software on the first bounce. Avoid owning capex-heavy platforms into prints unless they quantify AI revenue. Change the call when a guidance-cut stock rallies on the day — that would mark capitulation in the punished cohort.

Attention Gap: Venezuela coverage is dominated by politics, but the operating signal is concrete: Washington issued a license facilitating oil and gas exploration and production in the country Reuters [Feb 10]. Service companies — which supply rigs, completions and equipment before any new barrel flows — are the first-order beneficiaries, yet the discussion stays on the majors.

Exposure & Risk: Express via SLB, Halliburton and Baker Hughes or the OIH basket, with Chevron as the integrated proxy — CVX is up 13.39% over 20 sessions at 185.82 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11). Risks: license reversals, payment risk on a state counterparty, and the EIA's lower-price outlook U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) (.gov) [Feb 11], which could cap upstream budgets.

Attention Gap: Attention is uniformly negative — the narrative is AI eating software — but JPMorgan strategists say AI fears on software stocks are overblown Bloomberg.com [Feb 10]. Microsoft is down 14.09% over 20 sessions at 404.37 and Oracle 22.31% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11): profitable platforms with proprietary data are being sold alongside seat-based point solutions.

Exposure & Risk: Build slowly in large, cash-generative platforms (Microsoft, Salesforce) or IGV rather than small-cap SaaS. Risks: another model release that broadens the disruption, and credit contagion — Morgan Stanley's warning on a $1.5 trillion credit market Reuters [Feb 10] means forced selling by lenders is possible. Add only on days when bad news fails to make new lows.

Market Context: Bitcoin's prior completed daily close was 66,991.97, down 2.62% on the day and 25.12% over 20 sessions; ether closed at 1,940.62, down 34.21%, and solana at 79.25, down 38.22% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11). The equity proxies are worse: COIN fell 5.73% to 153.20 and is down 39.37% over 20 sessions, MSTR is down 27.12% and IBIT 28.52% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11).

New / Most Important: Stress has moved from prices into crypto credit: lender BlockFills suspended withdrawals amid the faltering bitcoin price Reuters [Feb 11]. The damage is reaching brokers — Robinhood's Q4 revenue missed Yahoo Finance [Feb 11] — and the deeper drawdowns in ether and solana show leverage being flushed from the higher-beta tokens first.

Playbook: Stay underweight; do not buy the dip until bitcoin reclaims the $71,000 area CoinDesk flagged as fresh resistance CoinDesk [Feb 09]. Prefer IBIT over COIN and MSTR, where equity and balance-sheet leverage amplify drawdowns. Add only if no other lender follows BlockFills Reuters [Feb 11]; cut further on a second withdrawal halt or a daily close below 66,991.97 that fails to recover within a week (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11).

Rates & Dollar: DXY closed at 96.83, down 2.32% over 20 sessions; TLT is up 1.76% over five sessions at 88.06, HYG is down 0.26% over 20 sessions at 80.83 and LQD 0.05% at 110.70 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11). The 10Y at 4.18% and the 30Y at 4.82% are little changed over 20 observations, with the 30Y−10Y spread at +64 bps (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-11). The yuan's climb to its strongest since 2023 amid a report on Treasuries Bloomberg.com [Feb 09] adds an official-sector reason for dollar weakness.

Credit Check: Supply is the story: Alphabet sold almost $32 billion of bonds to fund AI Bloomberg.com [Feb 10], and investment-grade prices barely moved, with LQD down 0.05% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11). The crack is in private markets: Morgan Stanley warns the software selloff may pose a risk to a $1.5 trillion credit market Reuters [Feb 10]. Public investment-grade credit is fine; private loans to software borrowers are where the marks will come.

Portfolio Implication: Keep credit in investment grade and short-dated high yield; avoid BDCs and private-credit vehicles with heavy software exposure. Hold gold as the dollar-diversification hedge — GLD is up 10.91% over 20 sessions at 467.63 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11) — and add non-US equity, where Europe and Asia lead fund inflows Reuters [Feb 06]. Change the call if a hot CPI lifts the dollar and real yields together.

What Is Priced: After payrolls rose 130,000 CNBC [Feb 11], economists expect the Fed to hold through May Reuters [Feb 11]. The 2Y at 3.52% still yields less than the 3M bill at 3.70% (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-11), so the curve continues to price some easing. The delayed report lands on Friday Investopedia [Feb 11].

Conditional Expression: Hot core print: sell 2Y Treasuries, rotate from homebuilders and small caps into energy and staples retail, and buy the dollar against the euro. Soft print: add duration via TLT, buy homebuilders and IWM, and sell the dollar against the yen. IWM is up only 1.38% over 20 sessions at 264.95 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11), so a soft print has the most room to run there.

Risk: The release was delayed, and data collected around the shutdown carry larger revision risk, so a single month can mislead. The bigger risk is a mixed print — firm services, soft goods — that leaves the pause intact and markets range-bound, with VIX at 17.65 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11) offering little cushion for a disappointment.

What Is Priced: Oil carries a modest risk premium: Brent closed at 69.40, up 6.0% over 20 sessions, and WTI at 64.63, up 5.69% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11). The Pentagon is preparing a second aircraft carrier to deploy to the Middle East WSJ [Feb 11] while diplomacy continues; the market prices a standoff, not a supply disruption.

Conditional Expression: Escalation: own XLE and Brent call spreads, short airlines. De-escalation: the premium deflates toward the EIA's lower-price path U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) (.gov) [Feb 11] — sell energy into strength and rotate into airlines and refiners. Use options rather than adding to energy equity, which is already up 16.98% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11).

Risk: The asymmetry is timing: a carrier deployment WSJ [Feb 11] is a signal, not a decision, and oil can drop sharply on any sign of talks. Gold, up 10.86% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11), is the cleaner hedge if escalation coincides with weaker risk appetite.

Catalyst & Thesis: Applied Materials reports with traders bracing for a sizable post-earnings move Investopedia [Feb 11]. The demand signal going in is strong: TSMC's board approved a record $45 billion package for new fabs Tom's Hardware [Feb 10], and the memory shortage argues for more DRAM capacity. We expect orders and guidance to beat on leading-edge logic and DRAM tools.

Price Hurdle & Risk: No card price; the hurdle is guidance strong enough to offset weaker China demand, where SMIC describes 'crisis mode' Nikkei Asia [Feb 11]. With SOXX up 9.03% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11), expectations are high — a beat with a cautious China outlook could still sell off.

Catalyst & Thesis: JPMorgan cut its Coinbase price target to $290 ahead of earnings CoinDesk [Feb 10], and the peer read-across is poor: Robinhood's Q4 revenue missed estimates Yahoo Finance [Feb 11]. With bitcoin down 25.12% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11), transaction revenue and guidance are at risk.

Price Hurdle & Risk: COIN closed at 153.20, down 39.37% over 20 sessions from 252.69 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11). The risk to the short is that much bad news is priced; a bitcoin recovery through $71,000 CoinDesk [Feb 09] or strong subscription revenue would force covering. Cover on a close back above the 20-session reference.

Catalyst & Thesis: McDonald's earnings beat estimates as the chain's value push paid off CNBC [Feb 11]. In a consumer sector where Amazon sold off on capex and December retail sales stalled Reuters [Feb 10], a restaurant gaining traffic with value is a share-taker, not a victim.

Price Hurdle & Risk: No card price. The risk is that a firmer labour market — unemployment fell to 4.3% CNBC [Feb 11] — lifts wage costs and squeezes franchisee margins. Own on post-results pullbacks; exit if traffic gains fade in the next quarter.

Observed Attention: Memory is retail's AI trade of the month: 24/7 Wall St. says Micron stock can't stop going up and Goldman Sachs knows exactly why 24/7 Wall St. [Feb 09]. MU rose 9.94% in the prior session to 410.34 and 21.36% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11).
Motivation & Bias: A simple shortage story plus visible momentum — recency bias treats peak-cycle pricing as permanent, even though memory is the most cyclical corner of semis.

Instrument & Risk: Prefer MU stock or call spreads to leveraged single-stock products. The risk is a supply response from rivals — the classic end of a memory upcycle — and Micron's 20-session reference of 338.13 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11) shows how far a reversal could run.

Observed Attention: Yahoo Finance describes gold as a safe haven that is trading like a meme stock Yahoo Finance [Feb 07]. SLV jumped 4.29% in the prior session to 76.56 but is down 2.6% over 20 sessions, while GLD is up 10.91% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11).
Motivation & Bias: Debasement fear and FOMO after record prices; retail treats a hedge as a momentum trade, which is how hedges become crowded positions.

Instrument & Risk: Use unlevered GLD or SLV and size as a hedge, not a trade. Silver's 20-session decline despite gold's rally shows how quickly the speculative layer reverses, and leveraged products decay in that kind of chop.

Observed Attention: Hong Kong retail investors snapped up bitcoin amid the crypto crash South China Morning Post [Feb 06] even as prices kept sliding — bitcoin is down 5.05% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11).
Motivation & Bias: Anchoring on prior highs and averaging down; the dip-buyer trusts that the four-year cycle guarantees a recovery.

Instrument & Risk: Use IBIT rather than MSTR, which is down 27.12% over 20 sessions at 126.07 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-11) and adds balance-sheet leverage. Size small and wait for the credit stress shown by BlockFills' withdrawal halt Reuters [Feb 11] to clear.
Observed Attention: Forbes asks whether Reddit's 36% drop is an overreaction Forbes [Feb 09] — a platform retail traders use daily has become one they debate buying.
Motivation & Bias: Familiarity bias and the anchor of the old high; holders treat the drawdown as a discount on a business they see every day.

Instrument & Risk: Use stock rather than short-dated options and add only if the shares hold their post-earnings lows. The risk is AI search eroding traffic and the broader de-rating of internet platforms, which has not ended.
